assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hijacking the ubiquitin-proteasome system with bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues is a genuinely new chemical modality that makes previously undruggable proteins addressable. It is the kind of game-changer with demonstrated consequences that I look for: a simple chemical idea (induced proximity) now carried into many clinical programs.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies introduced the PROTAC concept (c. 2001), and Handa's identification of cereblon as the target of thalidomide-type glues explains the molecular-glue branch. Ciulli, Gray and others made major later contributions; the three-person limit forces a hard choice and I am relying on recalled priority rather than verification.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades old, with multiple independent degraders in advanced clinical trials and structural understanding of ternary complexes. Clinical approvals for PROTACs are still pending, so timing is arguably slightly early for the PROTAC branch but well supported for the glue branch.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should centre on PROTACs or on molecular glues/cereblon biology, which have different originators.
No approved PROTAC drug as of my knowledge, so clinical impact is not fully proven.
Allocation among Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli and Gray is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors convert one base into another without double-strand breaks, a conceptually elegant and straightforward chemical solution that extends genome editing to precise point mutation correction. Chemistry-driven protein engineering with direct therapeutic consequences.
assessment.attribution: David R. Liu is clearly the decisive originator, with Komor and Gaudelli as the lead trainees on cytosine and adenine base editors; a single-laureate or shared-with-prime-editing framing is clean and fits the three-person limit.
assessment.maturity: First published 2016-2017 and already in clinical trials with early patient benefit reported; independent replication is broad. Genome editing was recognised in 2020, so the committee may see this as a follow-on, but the new chemistry is distinct.
uncertainties: Possible reluctance to reward a second genome-editing prize so soon after CRISPR-Cas9 (2020).
Overlap with prime editing (B011), which could be bundled or treated separately.
Long-term clinical safety and efficacy data are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing-by-synthesis transformed biology and medicine by collapsing the cost of sequencing by orders of magnitude; the chemistry of reversible terminators and clonal amplification on surfaces is the core invention. Unquestionable lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman founded the Solexa chemistry and single-molecule clustering approach; Rothberg's 454 pyrosequencing platform was the first commercial NGS system. Mayer, Ju and others contributed, and priority among the platforms is the main difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: two decades of ubiquitous use and many independent platforms. If anything it is overdue, though some may regard it as technology or medicine rather than chemistry.
uncertainties: Allocation across competing platforms (Solexa, 454, Lynx/Mayer, Ju's terminators).
Sanger sequencing was recognised in 1980, and some members may view NGS as primarily technological.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took solar cell efficiencies from a few percent to above 25 percent in about a decade, a new class of semiconductor with unusual defect tolerance. A real material game-changer, though not yet a commercial one.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitised cell in 2009, Park the first solid-state ~9 percent device, and Snaith the efficient planar and mesostructured devices; Kanatzidis, Grätzel and Seok are also strong claimants, so the three-person limit is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency and fundamental understanding are well confirmed across laboratories, but long-term operational stability, lead toxicity and manufacturing at scale remain unresolved, which argues for waiting.
uncertainties: Stability and commercial viability are not yet shown.
Allocation among six credible names; Grätzel's dye-sensitised precedent complicates credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics unified electronic structure and dynamics, enabling first-principles simulation of condensed-phase chemistry, from water to reactions in solution and solids. It is foundational for ab initio simulation and fits my field's view that good theory must connect quantitatively to experiment.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 paper is the clean two-person origin; credit is well defined. Parrinello also appears in the metadynamics and machine-learning-potential entries, which could affect how a theory prize is configured.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of use and extensive independent validation, including known limitations such as DFT functional accuracy. Timing is very mature and the computational chemistry prize area is ready for another recognition after 2013 and 1998.
uncertainties: Whether a prize would be framed as Car-Parrinello alone or alongside metadynamics/machine-learned potentials.
I have a professional stake in simulation methodology and must avoid favouring my own field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape and funnel theory solved the conceptual puzzle of how proteins fold on biologically relevant time scales (Levinthal paradox), tying statistical mechanics to experimental kinetics. Deep conceptual influence on biophysics and protein design.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes, Bryngelson and Onuchic developed the funnel and minimal frustration picture; Dill formulated the hydrophobic collapse perspective; Fersht provided key experimental phi-value analysis. Credit is spread, and the choice among theory and experiment is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Concepts are well established and widely used, though the connection to quantitative prediction is largely retrospective; AlphaFold's 2024 recognition shifted the protein-folding conversation toward structure prediction.
uncertainties: Whether the theoretical or experimental contributions (Fersht) should be weighted.
Impact is more conceptual than a single concrete invention, weakening the 'game-changer' test somewhat.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative mass-spectrometry proteomics (shotgun, SILAC/label-free, targeted methods) turned protein identification and quantification into a routine whole-proteome measurement, which underlies much of systems biology and biomarker work.
assessment.attribution: Mann, Yates and Aebersold are the broadest leaders; Hunt, Gygi and Heck made decisive contributions in specific methods. Ionization methods were recognised in 2002, so the proteomics workflow may be seen as an extension.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently validated. Possible concern that this is a collection of methods rather than a single sharply defined discovery.
uncertainties: Overlap with 2002 prize and with Orbitrap (B018) and native MS (B021).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically encoding unnatural amino acids through orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs lets chemists install new functionality into proteins in living cells, a simple and powerful concept with broad use in protein engineering and chemical biology.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first eukaryotic and bacterial systems; Chin extended to multiple codons and eukaryotes, and Yokoyama and Mehl contributed important systems. Priority between Schultz and Chin lineages is a recognised issue.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of use and many independent applications, with therapeutic proteins using unnatural amino acids now in trials; broad consequences are still emerging.
uncertainties: Credit among Schultz, Wang, Chin, Mehl and Yokoyama.
Applications are less transformative than those of higher-ranked candidates so far.
